hints.title: Translate the seating requirement
hints.body: Every empty chair must already have an occupied chair beside it. Otherwise the next person could choose an empty chair with both neighbours empty.
hints.recap: No run of three empty chairs is allowed.
hints.pitfall: The question asks for a suitable arrangement, not that every arrangement of that many people works.
hints.pause: How many chairs can one occupied chair cover, counting itself?

recall.reminder: Translate an extremal arrangement into a bound before constructing an example.

hints.title: Obtain an integer lower bound
hints.body: Imagine marking each occupied chair and the chairs immediately beside it. Compare the number of marks one occupant can provide with the total number of chairs that must be covered.
hints.recap: A coverage bound limits how small an arrangement can be.
hints.pitfall: Coverage can overlap, so <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mn>3</mn><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> is an upper bound on coverage, not automatically exact.
hints.pause: Write an inequality for the number of occupied chairs and convert it to an integer bound.

recall.reminder: A lower bound on an integer count must be rounded up.

hints.title: Show the bound is attainable
hints.body: Try distributing the occupied chairs as evenly as possible. Use your coverage bound to decide which gaps are allowed and check the gap across the circular join.
hints.recap: A lower bound becomes a minimum only when an arrangement achieves it.
hints.pitfall: The last chair is adjacent to the first chair.
hints.pause: Construct an arrangement using your proposed minimum and check every empty chair.

recall.reminder: A lower bound becomes a minimum only when an arrangement achieves it.

solution:
If n chairs are occupied, each occupant can account for at most three chairs: their own and the two adjacent chairs. For every empty chair to have an occupied neighbour, all 40 chairs must be covered, so 3n≥40 and n≥14.

Fourteen suffice: number the chairs around the circle and occupy 1,4,7,…,40. The gaps in this list contain two empty chairs each, and chairs 40 and 1 are adjacent across the circular join. Every empty chair is therefore next to an occupied one.

The lower bound and construction agree.

Answer D: 14.
knowledgePattern: Prove a circular seating minimum using coverage and a construction
